holidays.name: National Blueberry Popsicle Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the frozen, fruity delight of the blueberry popsicle. It's an excuse to cool off at the tail end of summer with a purple-tongued treat.
holidays.origin: Like many food observances, it comes from the informal world of national food days, popularized by food brands and online calendars rather than any official proclamation.
holidays.funFact: Popsicles were reportedly invented by accident in 1905 when an 11-year-old named Frank Epperson left a cup of soda powder and water with a stirring stick outside on a freezing night.

holidays.name: National Beer Lover's Day
holidays.description: A day for hop enthusiasts to raise a glass and appreciate the craft, history, and variety of beer, from crisp lagers to hazy IPAs.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance promoted by the beer community and calendar sites, it gives suds fans a reason to visit local breweries and try something new.
holidays.funFact: Beer is one of the oldest fermented beverages in the world, and ancient Sumerians even had a hymn to Ninkasi, the goddess of beer, that doubles as a recipe.

holidays.name: V-J Day Anniversary (Victory over Japan Day)
holidays.description: Marks the formal Japanese surrender aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay in 1945, ending World War II. It is commemorated with ceremonies and reflection in various countries.
holidays.origin: The surrender document was signed on September 2, 1945, and some nations, including the United States, have marked the date as the formal end of the war.
holidays.funFact: The signing ceremony on the USS Missouri used two copies of the Instrument of Surrender, and the ship is now a museum at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.

holidays.name: World Coconut Day
holidays.description: A tropical celebration of the coconut, the multitasking nut-fruit-seed that gives us water, milk, oil, and fiber. Fans crack one open and honor the 'tree of life.'
holidays.origin: Established by the Asian and Pacific Coconut Community (APCC), which was founded on September 2, 1969, to support coconut-producing countries.
holidays.funFact: A coconut is botanically classified as a drupe, which means it's not a true nut, and coconuts can float across oceans for thousands of miles to colonize far-off beaches.

holidays.name: Fiji's Day of the Rotuman Language? No, Actually: National Crazy Hat Day Alternative—Name Your Car Day
holidays.description: A playful day to give your trusty vehicle a name, whether it's Herbie, Betsy, or Sir Rusts-a-Lot. Because your car has been through a lot with you.
holidays.origin: A whimsical, unofficial observance that circulates on fun-holiday calendars, rooted in the long tradition of people personifying their vehicles.
holidays.funFact: Naming vehicles has a long tradition: sailors have named ships for centuries, and surveys suggest a large share of car owners name their cars.
